extracted.intended_audience: Catholic faithful and clergy preparing to celebrate or receive the Eucharist
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and devotional guidance on how priests and laypeople should prepare for, celebrate, and worthily receive the Eucharist; includes prayers, examinations of conscience, and prescriptions for priestly conduct. Focused on interior disposition and external duties connected to Mass and Communion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent reception of Communion
rubrics_metrics.description: Qu'il est utile de communier souvent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent approach to the sacrament is necessary because the soul needs this 'doux aliment' to sustain life and prevent spiritual decline; one should 's'approcher de vous souvent, et que vous vous receviez comme le soutien de ma vie' and receive at 'les temps convenables' rather than abstaining too long and abandoning resolutions. Even if not disposed daily, take care to approach at suitable times to partake of this great grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper preparation before receiving
rubrics_metrics.description: S'éprouver soi-même avant de manger le pain et de boire le calice du Seigneur; se préparer par la pénitence, le recueillement, la prière, et la confession fréquente.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must examine the conscience, have contrition, make sincere confession (if time permits), and pray and recollect oneself so as to receive fruitfully. But avoid staying away from the Table out of false respect or excessive fear — approach humbly like the Publican rather than proudly like the Pharisee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility and right interior disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Approcher avec un coeur rempli du sentiment de son indignité, pénétré de miséricorde et embrasé d'amour; aller comme le Publicain, 'les yeux baissés vers la terre'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain profound humility, awareness of personal unworthiness, but trust in Christ's mercy; avoid spiritual pride and hypocritical thanksgiving that compares oneself favorably to others. Ask God to clothe and sanctify the soul so one may be admitted to the feast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm faith in the Real Presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Croire sans hésiter que vous êtes ici présent dans ce Sacrement, et comme Dieu et comme homme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Believe more in the omnipotence of God than in the evidence of the senses; acknowledge that the sacrament is the true Body and Blood of Christ — this faith is necessary to approach the altar with proper reverence and to receive the spiritual fruits of Communion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving worthily to obtain abundant grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Dieu répand des grâces abondantes en ceux qui communient dignement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who receive with fervor, faith, and right disposition are strengthened: vices are healed, passions repressed, temptations dissipated or weakened, grace increased, virtues grown, faith and hope fortified, and love enflamed. The Eucharist is described as 'source de toute consolation intérieure' and a remedial food for spiritual weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine conscience thoroughly (detailed faults list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avant de toucher et recevoir le corps de Jésus-Christ, le prêtre (and faithful) doit s'approcher avec humilité et examiner soigneusement sa conscience; avoir une vive douleur de tous ses péchés et déplorer en particulier les fautes quotidiennes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives an extensive inventory of faults to examine (inclination to sin from youth, inattention, curiosity for novelties, avarice, intemperance in food and drink, negligence in prayer and offices, anger, harshness, inconstancy, sterility of good works, etc.). After confessing, one must form a firm resolution to amend and offer oneself as an oblation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly fitness and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Les prêtres, validement ordonnés dans l'Église, ont seuls le pouvoir de célébrer et de consacrer; le prêtre doit être orné de toutes les vertus et donner l'exemple d'une vie pure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only validly ordained priests may consecrate the Eucharist; priests must live irreproachably, be faithful in offering the sacrifice with fervor, be set apart from common ways, wear sacred vestments with the signs of the Cross to remember Christ's Passion, and practise continual prayer and intercession. Their duties are proportionate to their high vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer oneself wholly (oblation/resignation)
rubrics_metrics.description: S'offrir à Dieu sans réserve: 'offrez-vous ensuite, avec une pleine résignation... en l'honneur de mon nom, m'abandonnant entièrement le soin de votre corps et de votre âme'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The faithful should offer themselves as a perpetual holocaust in union with Christ's sacrifice; true oblation is not merely external acts but surrender of all affections and will to God. Without total self-giving, union with Christ through the sacrament is incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scrupulosity that prevents reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Prendre garde à ne se pas tenir éloigné de la Table sainte par un faux respect et une crainte excessive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While sincere preparation is necessary, one must not let exaggerated fear or scruples keep one from receiving the sacrament that Christ invites with 'Venez'; rely on God's mercy and come humbly rather than refusing the gifts of the Redeemer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sacraments and prayer for communal/personal needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Se servir des sacrements (confession, Eucharistie) et de la prière pour obtenir la consolation, la guérison des vices et l'augmentation de la grâce; prier et offrir pour autrui ('je vous offre aussi... les besoins de mes parents...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Eucharist and confession are means by which God 'console avec abondance en leurs tribulations', fortifies the weak, and sanctifies. The faithful are encouraged to offer Communion and prayers for the living and the dead, for relatives and benefactors, and to intercede for others' needs as part of their oblation.
